class.name: Pawn
class.brief_description: Makes its parent possessable: the framework's half of a playable thing.
class.description: Add it as a child of the node a player drives. It is a child rather than the root because the root is whatever the game needs - a [CharacterBody3D], an [Area2D], a [RigidBody3D] - and that choice belongs to the game; everything here works on [method get_pawn_root]. Override [code]_setup_input_component[/code] to bind actions, [code]_possessed[/code] and [code]_unpossessed[/code] to react to a controller taking it over. [method add_movement_input] and [method consume_movement_input_vector] keep "what the player asked for" separate from how the pawn moves. In a networked game the server drives the pawn and [member replicate_transform] mirrors where it ended up; guard movement with [method has_authority] so the same script is correct in every net mode. [method get_local_role] says what this copy is: [constant World.ROLE_AUTHORITY], [constant World.ROLE_AUTONOMOUS_PROXY] for the player driving it, or [constant World.ROLE_SIMULATED_PROXY] for everyone else.

method.name: _gather_movement_input
method.description: Called on the physics tick, immediately before the movement input is taken out. This is where [method add_movement_input] belongs. Reading input from [method Node._process] instead is not wrong, but it accumulates once per rendered frame while movement consumes once per physics frame, so the vector's length depends on how many frames happened to fit - which is what the clamp in [CharacterMovementComponent] exists to survive. Gathering here is exactly once per tick, so an analog stick keeps its magnitude and the clamp never has to do anything.

method.name: _get_replicated_properties
method.description: Override to add your own properties to what is kept in step across peers. Return their names; the framework attaches the synchronizer, so a project places no [MultiplayerSynchronizer] of its own.

method.name: _possessed
method.description: Override to react to being taken over - enabling behaviour, showing a nameplate.

method.name: _setup_input_component
method.description: Override to bind this pawn's input actions. [b]Called on possession, not from [code]_ready[/code][/b] - binding earlier is the single most common way for input to silently do nothing.

method.name: _unpossessed
method.description: Override to react to being let go.

method.name: add_movement_input
method.description: Accumulates a direction to move in this frame, scaled by [param scale]. It does not move anything: the pawn's own code takes the total out with [method consume_movement_input_vector] and applies it however it likes, which keeps [i]what the player asked for[/i] separate from [i]how it moves[/i]. In 2D, pack the axes into the [Vector3] and read back the ones you need.

method.name: consume_movement_input_vector
method.description: Reads the accumulated direction and clears it. Call it once per frame, where the movement is applied.

method.name: gather_movement_input
method.description: Calls [method _gather_movement_input]. Invoked by [CharacterMovementComponent] once per simulated step; a game has no reason to call it.

method.name: get_controller
method.description: The controller currently driving this pawn, or null.

method.name: get_local_role
method.description: What this peer may do with this pawn - see [enum World.NetRole]. Note that [b]authority is not ownership[/b]: the server has authority over every pawn, including one a client owns.

method.name: get_owner_peer_id
method.description: The connection this pawn answers to, through its controller.

method.name: get_pawn_root
method.description: The node this [Pawn] makes possessable - its parent. That is the [RigidBody2D], [CharacterBody3D] or whatever else the scene is built around, and it is what gameplay code almost always wants rather than the [Pawn] node itself.

method.name: get_pending_movement_input_vector
method.description: Reads the accumulated direction without clearing it.

method.name: get_player_state
method.description: The replicated data for the player driving this pawn, or null when nobody is.

method.name: get_remote_role
method.description: The mirror image of [method get_local_role].

method.name: get_world
method.description: The world this pawn belongs to.

method.name: has_authority
method.description: True on the server, and in a game with no peer at all. Guard movement with it: the server decides where a pawn is, and elsewhere it is only shown.

method.name: is_bot_controlled
method.description: Whether an [AIController] drives this pawn.

method.name: is_locally_controlled
method.description: True where the human driving this pawn is sitting - [b]the only place that may read input for it[/b].

method.name: is_player_controlled
method.description: Whether a [PlayerController] drives this pawn rather than an [AIController].

method.name: setup_input_component
method.description: Runs the input-binding hook. The [PlayerController] calls this on possession; override [method _setup_input_component] instead of calling it.

members.member: Whether possession makes the pawn's camera current, where the player is sitting. [b]Turn it off for a game filmed by a camera the level owns[/b] - otherwise the pawn quietly steals the view, and without a camera on the pawn you pay for a recursive search that finds nothing and warns.
The local player that takes this pawn over as soon as it is in the tree. [constant AUTO_POSSESS_DISABLED] means nothing happens on its own, which is what a pawn the game mode spawns wants.
The camera to make current on possession. Empty means search the pawn recursively for one.
Set when the framework spawns the pawn, and part of its node name, so the same pawn is addressed the same way on every peer.
Mirrors the root's position and rotation from the server. Turn it off for a pawn whose movement is driven some other way.

signal.name: unpossessed
signal.description: The controller let this pawn go.

constants.constant: Nothing possesses this pawn on its own. The default, and what a pawn spawned by the game mode wants.
